mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% indicates a significant weakening in aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained high unemployment rate rises above 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in PAYEMS and a fall in UNRATE indicates a situation where the labor market is expanding but unemployment is rising, signaling structural shifts or underemployment; this ambiguity often precedes market volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases (contradictory signal)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS rises and UNRATE rises simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in HOUST and a decline in RSAFS signals weakening consumer housing demand despite elevated housing inventory, which typically precedes softening in broader consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases while RSAFS decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST rises and RSAFS falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent low CPIAUCSL below 2% for six consecutive months, combined with low FEDFUNDS, signals a prolonged period of monetary accommodation and low inflation, which historically supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 2% for 6 consecutive months and FEDFUNDS < 2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of low CPIAUCSL (<2%) and low FEDFUNDS (<2%) for six months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between quarterly GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 20-day forward returns; higher GDP growth signals improved corporate earnings and supports positive returns regardless of regime.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between quarterly GDPC1 growth and S&P 500 20-day forward returns in out-of-sample walk-forward testing.
